items.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: It comes from early Duke and Spike Jones and a lot of other stuff if you don’t mind.

ctx.x: Because as you describe your own writing that sometimes things will come out of experience, later.

That’s it. I still have pratfalls in my writing. There’s Chaplinesque, and the old Keystone Cops and all that stuff is part of my early training. And it’s always been there. I have never been able, nor would I want to try to eliminate it or eradicate it from my experience, and when people ask me what is that, you know, I could be playing what they call “free” or “avante garde” and they say, “Well where did you — where did this stuff come from?” And I said, “It comes from early Duke and Spike Jones and a lot of…
Well you’ve, over the years, played with some pretty fierce saxophone players too.
